correctness.rationale: Starting from Walnut identity at integer oversampling, the scalar multiplier is an exact geometric series. Direct split integration derives H(s)=(R exp(-rs)-r exp(-Rs))/(R-r). Periodization and a distributional second-derivative bound yield uniform Bernoulli spatial curvature plus the positive first shift-correlation contribution. The resulting 3 two-sided deficit expansions are uniform near critical scale. Compactness and contrast of d_a plus the nonconstant autocorrelation Fourier series force all global optimizers into a logarithmic window. The normalized limiting costs are strictly convex coercive exponentials with unique minima, yielding all three loglog shifts and penalty profiles. Finite numerical tests only supplement this proof; self-review the quantifiers for fixed r<R, normalization by n and all error terms.
